title: Water Ready: Rainwater Harvesting, Storage, and Water Independence for Any Home
description: Most water books are written for someone with five acres, a tractor, and a well permit already in hand. If that's not you, they leave you flipping past forty pages you can't use to find the three paragraphs that actually apply to your home. Water Ready starts differently. In ten minutes, a simple formula tells you exactly how many gallons your own roof can produce in a year — and sorts you into the right starting point before you spend a dollar. Renter with a balcony. Suburban homeowner with an HOA. Rural landowner with acreage. Off-grid cabin owner. Every chapter tells you upfront whether it applies to you, so you never waste time on advice built for someone else's property. Inside, you'll find: The 10-minute audit that turns your roof size and local rainfall into one real number A state-by-state legal quick reference, so you never guess whether you need a permit Three complete, priced systems — a $60 weekend rain barrel, a $350–$900 emergency reserve, and a $4,000–$8,000 whole-house cistern The exact line between water that's fine for your garden and water that's safe to drink Backup sources for when the sky won't cooperate — wells, springs, atmospheric generators, and greywater reuse A year-two maintenance schedule most water books skip entirely, covering winterizing, algae, mosquitoes, and leaks The twelve mistakes that cost other builders the most — with the real cost to fix each one Every project includes a real parts list with real prices, not vague suggestions. No padding, no history of ancient aqueducts, no twenty pages restating the same three filtration methods. description: The water stopped. And no one was coming to help. You turn on the tap. Nothing comes out. The city says it's a "boil water advisory." Then the plant failed. Then the National Guard shows up. It happened in Jackson. It happened in Flint. It is happening across the world — and it is getting worse. You have seen the headlines. But what have you actually done to prepare? Most people buy a case of bottled water and call it a plan. That's not a plan — that's a delay. description: Your Water Bill Is Rising. Your Tap Water Is Contaminated. Your Well Is Running Dry. You're paying more every month for water that's becoming less reliable — and less safe. The problem isn't just the cost. It's the creeping fear that one day, the water won't come at all. A drought. A broken pipe. A contamination scare. And suddenly, you're standing in a grocery store aisle, paying $1.50 per gallon for bottled water that's often no cleaner than what comes out of your tap. You've tried everything. Imagine turning on your faucet and knowing — with absolute certainty — that the water flowing out was produced in your own home, from the air you breathe. No municipal water bills. No plumbing required. No professional installation. Just a simple system you can build yourself in 1-3 hours with off-the-shelf parts. This book gives you the complete blueprint. How long could your household manage before the situation became serious? Perhaps you've already thought about storing more bottled water, drilling a deeper well, or investing in an expensive backup system. But there's another possibility worth understanding. title: Water Independence: A Practical Handbook for Rural, Cabin, and Homestead Water Systems
description: Water is the one problem off-grid living can't improvise around — and most people don't think about it until it's already too late. If you're buying rural land, building a cabin, or planning a homestead, this handbook walks you through every major decision about your water supply before you're stuck living with the consequences of skipping it: how much water your household actually needs, choosing between a well, a spring, or rainwater catchment, sizing and protecting your storage tanks through freezing winters, filtering and purifying water safely, pumping water without relying on grid power, handling greywater and septic systems the right way, and understanding water rights before you sign anything. Written in plain, non-technical language for people who aren't engineers or plumbers, this is the book you read before you call a well driller — not after something's gone wrong. No fluff, no filler, just a clear framework and the right questions to ask. title: Living Off-Grid: A Beginner-Friendly Guide To Solar, Water, and Food Independence
description: What would you do if the power went out, the water stopped flowing, or the grocery shelves started running low? Living Off-Grid gives beginners a practical starting point for solar power, clean water, food security, and simple self-reliance — without pretending you need to disappear into the wilderness. You don’t need years of experience, a remote piece of land, or expensive equipment to begin building a more independent life. You just need a clear plan, realistic steps, and a basic understanding of the systems that make off-grid living possible. This beginner-friendly guide shows everyday people how to think about off-grid living in a practical way. Whether your goal is to prepare for emergencies, reduce your dependence on fragile systems, or eventually transition into a more self-sufficient lifestyle, this book gives you a simple foundation to build from. Inside, you’ll discover how to: • Understand the core principles of off-grid living without getting lost in technical jargon • Explore beginner-friendly solar power options for energy independence • Plan for clean water through storage, filtration, and reliable backup systems • Grow food more sustainably and improve your long-term food security • Avoid common mistakes that can cost time, money, and frustration • Take realistic steps toward self-reliance, preparedness, and sustainability This isn’t a fear-based survivalist manual or a complicated technical textbook. It’s a clear, practical roadmap for people who want more control, more confidence, and more resilience in everyday life.
